While pedestrian identification (Pedestrian Identification, PedID) has advanced significantly, cross-domain PedID remains challenging due to significant distribution shifts between source and target domains. Most current methods employ domain adaptation strategies to address this, though they often overlook the issue of false positives resulting from out-of-target-domain images. Domain-specific fine-tuning is frequently cited as a solution; however, this approach fails to fully eliminate false positives because source domain labels cannot be completely discarded. In response, we introduce unsupervised domain-specific PedID re-ranking to effectively suppress these irrelevant results. Our approach treats re-ranking as an image retrieval problem, leveraging unsupervised cluster centers derived from target domain data. By employing an efficient retrieval mechanism, our re-ranking method can be seamlessly integrated into various domain adaptation domain-specific PedID schemes. Comprehensive experiments across three prominent public datasets demonstrate that our proposed method consistently outperforms competing techniques.

This paper introduces a novel low-bitrate audio upconversion framework leveraging deep learning, designed to perform spectral domain upconversion through a two-stage pipeline. Initially, audio signals are converted into the corresponding mono grayscale image domain. Subsequently, a dedicated upconversion model restores these signals within a higher spectral domain. Evaluations on the enhanced free audio dataset exhibit substantial improvements across critical for perceptual metrics, achieving an average relative gain reaching approximately 17.5 decibels relative to standard upconversion techniques.

In this academic paper, a novel low-bitrate audio enhancement framework is presented, employing a two-stage approach within the spectral domain that utilizes deep learning. This system transforms audio signals into their visual monochrome equivalent as the initial stage. The subsequent stage involves applying an upconversion neural network to restore these representations within a higher-frequency spectral field. Performance analysis on significantly expanded audio libraries demonstrates substantial enhancements in perceptual quality metrics, yielding an average relative gain near 17.5 decibels when benchmarked against conventional upconversion methodologies.

This study explores the repercussions of releasing a ball at a faulty location during ball-sport throwing, highlighting how an improper release point necessitates complex adjustments across the entire kinetic chain to redirect it toward target accuracy. Through simulations of inaccurate underhand and overhand overthrows aimed at a central goal, varying only the initial release coordinates while maintaining standard motion trajectories and release velocities, the paper demonstrates that achieving a precise throw following a poor start requires upstream adjustments beginning well before the shoulder. Specifically, a 10-degree shift in shoulder rotation angle was identified as a critical factor. Furthermore, the research underscores the greater sensitivity associated with the overhand style compared to the underhand variety, revealing that the magnitude of upstream adjustments is directly correlated with the spatial deviation of the release point from the point of release generated by an ideal throw.

Neural machine translation (NMT) frameworks typically rely on sequential models to predict output sentences; however, this approach fails to fully leverage the inherent tree structure present within phrases and trees. This work addresses that gap by introducing a top-down, syntree-based decoder designed to complete a structured output using syntematic links. Drawing inspiration from the sequential beam search algorithm, we propose a novel "link beam search" technique that maintains an active set of candidate links rather than individual full structures. By efficiently exploring candidate syntematic links during inference, our method achieves a more effective search strategy. Empirical evaluations on the IWSLT2016 dataset demonstrate that the system attains competitive BLEU scores of 41.1 while generating high-quality syntactic parse trees with an F1 measure of 79.6. Furthermore, an analysis of generated trees reveals that the top 50 candidate structures share an F1 average of 83.6, indicating that our decoder produces highly consistent and accurate structural candidates.

Accurate knowledge of reaction rates is crucial for deciphering the chemistry occurring in the interstellar medium. A fundamental component for deriving these kinetics in cold environments is a comprehensive understanding of the binding energy (BE) distribution between molecules and grain surfaces. While previous studies have frequently assumed a single, universal BE distribution, recent research indicates variability based on molecular identity, the specific site, and environmental factors. We introduce the Binding Energy Assessment (BEA) Platform, a dedicated database containing over 1000 BE distributions quantified via quantum chemistry calculations. Each molecule and its corresponding distribution are accessible through a simple web-based interface. Furthermore, a newly developed method has been proposed to characterize these distributions, addressing the complexities of multi-modal and skewed data sets. By facilitating the integration of diverse binding energy data and supporting future additions through the BEA Platform, we aim to lay the groundwork for constructing more reliable surface binding energies within grain-surface chemical models.

This work examines a non-uniform random walk within random multiplicative processes, incorporating a parameter-defined floor that cannot be surpassed by the resulting sample values. While this non-markovian behavior poses challenges, it is addressed by developing a closed-form expression for the probability density function (PDF) and mapping it to a corresponding cumulative distribution function (CDF). Furthermore, analytical and numerical exploration of the underlying stochastic differential equation (SDE) and its linked Fokker-Plank equation (FPE) provides an alternative SDE-based perspective. An analytical investigation also evaluates statistical descriptors, including characteristic and scaled characteristic functions. In parallel, an analytical framework is constructed to calculate key moments—such as the mean, variance, skewness, and higher central moments—and validates them against Monte Carlo simulations. These statistical measures, along with an analytical and practical application of the fitted SDE model to real-world financial time series, are presented via plots of PDF/CDF shapes, moment behavior under varying parameters, and characteristic function dynamics. Ultimately, this study offers both theoretical insights and practical utility for the analysis of random multiplicative processes and non-uniform stochastic processes in both mathematical and financial domains.

Assessing the depth of quantum circuits is crucial for managing quantum noise and establishing fault tolerance thresholds. However, existing measurement methods lack precision, particularly for circuits nearing the fault-tolerant limit. We introduce a novel, shallow diagnostic framework that identifies circuit regions with random Clifford circuit measurements. By calculating the average post-selection rate across these measures, our approach provides unbounded estimates of expectation values. Experimental results with intermediate-scale noisy devices demonstrate that our protocol is significantly more potent than prior methods. Specifically, in reconstructing the ground states of Ising models, our method maintains accuracy even as circuit complexity grows, without requiring additional qubits.

This work examines the constant-zero-level set of the reflection coefficient for the defocusing Davey-Stewartson II system. By defining two specific regions, $R_1$ and $R_2$, the analysis demonstrates that the coefficient remains bounded away from zero in $R_1$ and approaches zero in a weak sense within $R_2$. These conclusions are derived by utilizing the scattering data linked to the two-dimensional Schrödinger operator, the solution to the corresponding Lax pair at the origin, and the associated Green function. Notably, the behavior observed in $R_2$ aligns with the established findings for the two-dimensional Schrödinger data.

This work introduces the application of the Sibyl network to the categorical realm. A Sibyl network is a directed, weighted graph where each node represents an opinion; the associated commentaries are weighted by trust, and the strength of inter-node relationships reflects the degree of agreement or disagreement. We demonstrate that the stable comments produced by our robustified Sibylvariant offer significant enhancements in the accuracy of the categorical systems.

We present an issue-based framework for creating linear illustrations that align with existing ones, designed for potential adaptation to nonlinear cases. We validate this approach by proving its ability to generate linear illustrations capable of generalizing across multiple instances within a single domain and across different domains entirely, without requiring the use of activation functions.

Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models are surprisingly sensitive to degradation in performance, which can happen when they are extracted or quantized. To create low-resource Machine Translation (MT) systems, lightweight and efficient models are essential. However, utilizing full fine-tubing strategies for low-data scenarios is often not feasible because gathering large translation corpora is difficult. Consequently, applying quantization and extraction becomes a viable option to build these lightweight systems. Yet, the comparative stability of these two compression approaches, which is critical for low-data translation tasks, remains unclear. This study presents a comprehensive empirical analysis of how model quality in low-resource settings changes following post-training extraction and quantization extraction.

The findings indicate that for low-data translation tasks, model performance is more unstable after post-training extraction than after quantization. Furthermore, simple, robust post-training techniques can be employed to improve the final results. The authors also provide open-source code and models for both compressed and uncompressed versions, covering various low-resource language pairs.

This work presents a novel field-theoretic framework designed to rigorously determine the Lagrangian density governing non-holomorphic fields of complex type within a topological graph structure. By constructing this density, the study introduces the field equations of motion and derives the associated Einstein-like field equations. Furthermore, the study establishes corresponding expressions for an energy-momentum tensor, establishes a wave-like equation of motion, and provides a theoretical basis for a kinetic-like equation. Applying this formalism to the field of hypergraphs—specifically their non-homorphic, topological variants—yields an analytical solution for the solitary wave of a general hypergraph, whose effective mass and associated scalar field can subsequently be explicitly defined.

Deep learning architectures have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in biomedical tasks, including segmentation; however, gathering extensive labeled datasets remains a formidable hurdle. To mitigate this reliance, researchers have turned to techniques such as data augmentation and transfer learning. This study investigates a distinct approach by applying enhancement algorithms—specifically super-resolution, deblurring, and colorization—to training images within the context of pneumonia segmentation in chest X-rays superiors. Utilizing an improved U-Net architecture as an initial step, experiments were conducted on the ISICNIH Chest X-Ray dataset. Results indicate that employing these enhancement strategies reduces necessary labeled data compared to traditional methods. Specifically, achieving performance comparable to models trained on 100% of the labeled data could be attained using approximately 75% of the labeled through a combination of techniques. This finding is particularly impactful given that labeled data collection is time-consuming and often inaccessible in scenarios requiring specialized annotators like medical professionals who are in short supply across certain regions in addition to being costly. Although current captioning models excel at generating detailed descriptions, they often lack the ability to adhere to specific constraints when requested by users. This limitation renders them unsuitable for real-world scenarios where image captions must meet regulatory standards, such as avoiding prohibited objects or tones defined by corporate guidelines. This work introduces a new framework enabling captioning models to generate regulated descriptions tailored to user specifications. By leveraging pre-trained models and utilizing a training-free, instruction-following strategy, the proposed method employs an advanced prompting technique to ensure models strictly comply with various form, style, and content restrictions without retraining. Specifically, this approach enables models to reject inappropriate content entirely, such as depictions of people, and allows them to generate substitutions with permissible alternatives. Furthermore, these descriptions can be crafted to align with designated tones and styles, or modified to match specific vocabulary lists provided by the user. Empirical results indicate that this simple yet effective technique significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art methods across multiple dimensions of image captioning.

These weak labels guide the training of a novel network architecture capable of accurately localizing and segmenting viral lesions in CT images. Furthermore, the proposed DAG algorithm demonstrates superior performance compared to state-of-the-art methods in terms of accuracy on both normal and infected chest radiographs, showing that it outperforms CNN-based models relying on standard labeling methods.
